**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut). No blockers found. Below is what I built, ran and tried.

Head `d36f2381` already contains current `origin/main`, so the trial merge was a no-op. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is bumped 16 -> 17 for the camcraft-mcp skill line, as the process law requires.

### What looks good
- **One read path.** The GUI page (`state_tool_library.rs`), MCP `import_tool_library` and the script verb all go `parse_tool_library` -> `read_body` -> `ImportTools::with_holders`. `read_body` uses the same `ToolBodyDto::to_body` + `tool_body::fits` that `project::validate` uses, and the command checks `fits` again. I found no path that skips it. This branch has no `Update`/`Replace` modes and no drag-and-drop import.
- **No file reads from the body.** A placed-mesh body embeds its facets; `source` is a label only and is never opened. So there is no path-traversal or absolute-path surface.
- **Whole file or nothing.** Every body is judged during parsing, before the command exists. A refusal names the tool and leaves no tool and no history entry (pinned by `a_malformed_or_ill_fitting_body_refuses_the_file_by_name`).
- **Holders off.** Tools land with the holder cylinder from their own record. The status line and the MCP reply say "N holders in the file not imported" (`holders_left_out`), so the loss is named rather than silent. The skip identity is sound: a bare-landing tool matches on the record only, and a tool landing with a body must match the body too, otherwise it arrives as "Name (2)" and never overwrites the document's holder.
- **Format.** Stays `camcraft-tools/1`. Main's `tool_from_json` has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so an older build drops `body`. Export writes bodies, and export -> import -> export is byte-stable (pinned).
- **Prefs.** The toggle lives in the per-user prefs file (`importToolHolders`, written only when false), not in the project or the history.

### Local results (Windows, debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app `tool_library` | 13 passed |
| app `tool_library_holders` | 5 passed |
| app `view_prefs` | 7 passed |
| app `mcp` | 13 passed |
| ui `--lib tool_library` / `--lib structural` (CWD crates/ui) | 3 / 4 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Hostile-file probe.** This was a local test, not pushed, built on the suite's own `source()` fixture, with holders on:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Negative spun radius | refused by name |
| `r = 1e300` | refused by name |
| `z = 1e300` | refused ("larger than any tool a spindle carries") |
| Empty facets | refused by name |
| Zero-area facets | refused by name |
| Facets at 1e12 | refused by name |
| Facets reaching into the flutes | refused ("does not surround the tool axis") |
| A lathe placement on a milling tool | refused by name |
| 200,000 facets | refused in ~1 s, no hang |

None of these panicked.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Placement metadata is not checked on load.** A placed-mesh body with `"offset": -1e9`, `"offset": 1e300` or `"axis": [0,0,0]` is **accepted**, and the garbage is stored. The derived envelope comes from the facets, so the collision input itself is sound. This is the project loader's behaviour too (`tool_body::build` does not re-check the axis/offset that `tool_body::place` refuses), so it is not new here. Still, a file can now carry it into a document; a follow-up issue to check axis/offset in `build` (as `place` does) seems worthwhile.
- **Holders off still checks bodies.** A file whose body is bad is refused even when the bodies would be thrown away. That is conservative and fine; it may just surprise someone.
- `cam.importTools(path)` is fixed to holders on. That is documented in the decision file, and MCP has the flag.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs` (1933 lines) grows by 9 lines. It was already far over 400, so this is noted, not blocking.
- **Not exercised:** the GUI by hand (the checkbox and the persistence across restarts beyond `view_prefs`), and the release lanes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**main merged in (head 9a8b34af), #899's import modes combined with #889's holder bodies.** Still a draft.

How they fit together (decision file `docs/decisions/889-camtools-holder-body.md`, item 8):
- `ImportTools::with_options(world, library, mode, holders)` is the one command. `with_mode` means holders on and `with_holders` means Add mode. #899's `ImportMode`, `Step` plan and `change_refusal` gates are unchanged; the bodies ride on top of them.
- **Add**: works as this PR had it. The tool lands with the file body when holders is on and bare when it is off. When a body lands, a tool is only skipped if its record and its body (as the DTO) both match the document's.
- **Update / Replace, holders on**: a file body that differs from the document tool's body is a `Step::Change` like any other change, even when the tool record is identical. It goes through `change_refusal`, which now also checks that the body that will stand fits. The op stamp already includes the body, so the ops that use the tool go Stale exactly as they do after `SetToolBody` (pinned against a twin world). Undo restores the old body.
- **Update / Replace, holders off or no body in the file**: the document's body stays as it is and is never cleared silently. That body has to fit the incoming record, or the import is refused by tool name.
- Every file body is still fitted at command creation; a body that does not fit refuses the whole file by name.
- **Callers**: MCP `import_tool_library` takes both `mode` and `holders`. `cam.importTools(path, mode?, holders?)` takes both too, with `cam.d.ts` regenerated. The Tool library page shows the mode combo next to the "Import tool holders" checkbox.
- The camcraft-mcp skill line now documents both arguments, and `PROCESS_VERSION` goes to 19 (main's 18 + 1).
- `tool_import_modes.rs` (#1060) now builds its library tools with `LibraryTool::bare`, because the struct gained `body`. That is the only change in that file.
- A separate commit (`9a8b34af`) adds the same one-line `neck: None` fix as PR #1131 in `rotary_law_tests.rs` (#1146), so the app lib tests compile.

- `update_and_replace_take_a_changed_body_in_place_and_stale_the_op_as_set_tool_body_does`
- `a_changed_body_in_update_and_replace_takes_the_change_gates`

**Re-review after the merge of main: ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`, so it merges at the cut). No blockers.

Reviewed `d36f2381..ae46d12d`. That is two merges of main. The first, `25915250`, carries the hand-resolved hunks in `tool_import.rs`, `mcp/tools.rs`, `script/api.rs`, `script/mod.rs` and `tests/tool_import_modes.rs`, which I read hunk by hunk with `git show --cc`. The second, `ae46d12d`, changes only `PROCESS_VERSION`. I also trial-merged the head with current `origin/main` (`7e3c75f9`): it merged clean.

### How the merge composes
- The holders choice is the fourth parameter of one constructor, `ImportTools::with_options(world, lib, mode, holders)`. `new`, `with_mode` and `with_holders` are thin doors onto it with holders on and mode Add.
- The GUI (`state_tool_library.rs:63`, with `tool_import_mode` and `import_tool_holders`), MCP `import_tool_library` and `cam.importTools(path, mode?, holders?)` all call it.
- The defaults are the old behaviour on every surface: `mode` add, `holders` true. The camcraft-mcp skill row names both arguments and their defaults.
- In Update and Replace, a body change is a `Step::Change` carrying `(body before, file body)`. It passes `change_refusal`, which fits the body that will stand, and undo puts the old body back.
- A bodyless file entry, or holders off, leaves the document's body in place, and that body must fit the incoming record.

### Six combinations: what happens to a tool's body
Results from a local probe test (not pushed) built on the suite's own `source()` fixture: a drawn holder on `Six`, a meshed collar on `Four`, nothing on `Eight`.

| Mode | holders on | holders off |
|---|---|---|
| **Add** | A new tool arrives with its file body. Same record and same body: skipped. Same record but a different body (the file's holder over a bare document twin): arrives renamed `Four (2)` / `Six (2)` with its body, so the document's tool is never touched. | A new tool arrives bare (holder cylinder). The status line says "N holders in the file not imported". The skip compares the record only. |
| **Update** | A file body that differs replaces the document's in place: "2 updated (Four, Six) ... 2 with their holder". Undo brings the bare bodies back exactly. A file tool with **no** body and a changed record: "1 updated (Six)", and the document body is **kept** (verified bit-identical) and checked against the new record. | Records update and the document bodies are kept bit-identical: "2 updated ...; 2 holders in the file not imported". |
| **Replace** | As Update, plus a tool the file lacks is removed. | Changed tools keep their bodies. The bodied tool the file lacked (`Four`) was removed: "1 replaced (Six); 1 removed (Four); ... 1 holder in the file not imported". Undo restores `Four` **and its mesh body exactly**. |

Replace still refuses by name to remove a tool an operation uses (`tool_import_modes`, 9/9). Holders off therefore never strips a holder from a tool an operation uses: existing bodies are kept, and only unused tools can be removed. No collision input is lost silently.

### First-pass attacks, on the merged code
- **A bad body refuses the whole file in every mode.** The case was a file with a changed `Six` record and a broken `Four` body (facets reaching into the flutes). Add/on, Update/on, Replace/on, Update/off and Replace/off each refuse "tool 'Four': the tool body does not surround the tool axis ... (body refused)". In every case no record or body of the document changed and no history step was added. Bodies are judged while the file is parsed, before the command exists, and Update/Replace build their whole step list before anything is applied. **No half-applied Replace.**
- One undo step per import; undo restores bodies exactly for Update and Replace, as shown in the table.
- The hostile-body cases from the first pass all run through the same `parse_tool_library` -> `read_body` path, which this merge does not touch.

Every ui test file that names the import mode keeps main's count. No test was dropped.

### Other checks
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` reads **26** at the head; main reads 20.
- No snapshot PNG in the diff.
- No unwrap/expect/panic outside test code. The expects are in `src/egui_app/tests/tool_library_import.rs`.
- `tool_import.rs` is 385 lines and `tool_library_holders.rs` 382, both under 400.
- The Tool library page draws the mode combo (`pages.rs:998`) and the "Import tool holders" checkbox (`pages.rs:1005`) as separate rows, so neither hides the other.

### Notes (not blocking)
- Update+on with a bodyless file entry keeps the document body. That is the documented rule, but the status line says only "1 updated (Six)". Saying "(holder kept)" would make it visible.
- Update+off where the file differs from the document only in bodies is refused with "nothing to import: every tool in the library is already in the document". That is true, but it doesn't mention that holders were off. Naming that would help.
- First-pass note still stands: placement metadata (axis/offset) on a mesh body is not checked on load, the same as the project loader.
- **Not exercised:** the GUI by hand, and the release lanes.
